subject: Data description entry
notes: kb/Work PB488 LANDED. BOTH obligations of SR24 now have a site, in ONE place. (1) THE ASSOCIATION SENTENCE. BindEntries tracks `lastDescribed` -- the entry the level-88 entry IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWS, which is the rule's own subject -- instead of the level stack's top. The two coincide for every entry that opens or extends the level hierarchy and DIVERGE exactly for the entries that never enter the stack: a level-66 alias, a 13.10 constant entry, and the start of a section. Those divergences were the measured wrong answers. An 88 with no preceding entry describing a data item now draws COBOL1977 instead of being dropped silently and surfacing as a run-time NotImplementedCobolFeatureException. (2) THE EIGHT EXCLUSIONS are ONE TABLE, DataBinder.Sr24Exclusions -- one row per letter in the standard's order carrying the standard's words -- walked by ConditionalVariableExclusion, which returns the first matching row; the diagnostic COBOL1976 names the letter and quotes it. a) holds by construction (the 88 arm leaves `lastDescribed` alone, so a run of consecutive 88s shares one conditional variable, which is the rule's own plural) and the drift test verifies the predicate directly, since no DataItem in the forest carries level 88. b) the level-66 alias is now handed to the screen instead of stepped over (BindRenames returns it). c) ItemCategory.IsAlphanumericGroup (3.11's four-exclusion definition, 13.18.29.4 GR3 -- NOT 'IsGroup with GroupUsage.None', which over-included a variable-length and a strongly-typed group, kb/Work PB947) plus a subordinate at any depth whose usage is not DISPLAY -- a bit or national GROUP member counts, 13.18.29.4 GR1/GR2 treating it as an elementary item of usage bit/national. d) any group with a JUSTIFIED or SYNCHRONIZED subordinate, AND the group's OWN SYNCHRONIZED clause: 13.18.55.3 SR1 permits it there and 13.18.55.4 GR1 makes it a description of the members, and the binder does not propagate the flag, so a members-only screen would miss `01 G SYNCHRONIZED.` entirely. e) resolved through 13.18.60.3 SR4's OWN predicate Sr4PhraseOf -- SR4's six USAGE phrases produce exactly SR24 e)'s four classes -- reading the WRITTEN clause as well as the resolved Pic, because MESSAGE-TAG and FUNCTION-POINTER never gain a PicInfo. f) DataItem.IsAnyLength. g) the DECLARATION-side TypedefStrong, sharing UnderStrongTypeDeclaration with 13.18.60.3 SR14, whose second arm is the same words; the second arm is confined to GROUP items, so an elementary member of a strong template may still be a conditional variable. h) delegates to VariableLengthCompatibility.IsVariableLength (the group kind c) now subtracts, so c) and h) are disjoint), which IS 8.5.1.12.1's definition -- a group with a dynamic-length elementary item or a dynamic-capacity table subordinate -- NOT an occurs-depending-on group, which the standard names separately (13.18.12.3 SR2 lists the three side by side). IT IS A POST-BIND PASS (BindPipeline, PassPhase.UsageResolved) and could not be a test inside BindCondition: four of the eight exclusions ask about the conditional variable's SUBORDINATES, and a condition-name on a group is written BEFORE them, so parent.Children is still empty at bind time. UNGATED across the four editions -- COBOL-85's own condition-name rule states the same exclusions for every shape COBOL-85 can write, and the later letters name constructs their own introduction gates already refuse below their edition. OVER-REJECTION MEASURED: all 80 corpus programs that write a level-88 entry (conformance + NIST) were recompiled and not one draws COBOL1976/1977. kb/Work PB947 LANDED: the lettered quotation is now pinned per letter (each pb488-cond-var-* .err names its letter, because every letter produces COBOL1976) and a variable-length group holding a non-DISPLAY member quotes h) and never c).
